entries.title: The conformal-radius comparison must include the real boundary
entries.locator: arXiv:1502.04387v3, section 2, equation (2.2), printed p.4/PDF index 3. Versioned HTML and extracted PDF text checked 17 November 2026; no visual-PDF or journal comparison.
entries.claim: For a closed connected obstacle A in the upper half-plane, rho(w,A)/4 <= dist(w,A) <= rho(w,A).
entries.problem: Koebe and Schwarz bound distance to the whole boundary of the component of H minus A, which also includes the real line. Take A=R+10i and w=i: the component is the horizontal strip of height 10 and rho=(20/pi)sin(pi/10)<2, whereas dist(w,A)=9. Thus the printed upper comparison is false even when the component is simply connected.
entries.correction: For a simply connected component D use rho_D(w)/4 <= min(Im(w),dist(w,A)) <= rho_D(w). In particular rho<t<Im(w) implies dist(w,A)<t, while dist(w,A)<t/4 implies rho<t. The shrinking-neighbourhood proof uses a fixed bulk mark, so choose its radius below its height before the mesh limit. This repairs the cited use without changing Theorems 1 or 2.
entries.leanImpact: Any future conformal-radius interface must include the full domain boundary and a simply connected domain hypothesis. The local percolation application requires the explicit bulk-height restriction; site RSW and continuum density formulas remain inputs. The wiki gives the correction and the conditional lattice passage, but claims no compiled association or author confirmation.

resolution.summary: Measure distance to the whole component boundary and choose the bulk neighbourhood below its height.
resolution.impact: Repairs the shrinking-neighbourhood argument without changing either factorization theorem.
